The company has 90% of its Q4 revenue guidance already under contract, with consolidated Q4 revenue expected to be between $441 million and $456 million.
Following the completion of the Spain sale for approximately $135 million and Brazil sale for $15 million, total international divestitures will reach nearly $900 million.
The company completed a $2.05 billion senior secured note offering in August, extending weighted average debt maturity to 4.8 years and maintaining essentially flat annualized cash interest.
Corporate cost savings of $50 million announced at Investor Day remain on track, with approximately $40 million already having line of sight and expected to reach full run rate in 2026.
The newly acquired MTA roadside billboard contract assets in New York are ahead of internal projections and on track to be cash flow positive in year one.

Management outlined a value creation opportunity of approximately $1.7 billion for shareholders by year-end 2028, based on projected adjusted EBITDA growth of $115 million and debt paydown of approximately $400 million.

Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 13.1% from 12.3% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA up $3 million despite revenues declining $95 million primarily due to planned EUCOM contingency reduction.
Adjusted EPS was $0.96, down $0.05 year-over-year, mainly due to higher financing expenses from unconsolidated joint ventures, partially offset by lower share count from 2025 buybacks.

Adjusted operating cash flow totaled $119 million, up $28 million year-over-year, representing 98% adjusted OCF conversion, with net leverage at 2.3x trailing adjusted EBITDA (below the 2.5x ceiling).
STS Q1 book-to-bill ex-LNG was 1.2x (third consecutive quarter above 1.0x), backlog ended at approximately $4.7 billion (up 9% YoY), and work under contract covers ~67% of 2026 STS revenue guidance.

STS Q1 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 21.9% (up ~70 bps), but underlying margin excluding the LNG project contribution was 16.1%, with management guiding to ~15% base business margins going forward as LNG rolls off into early 2027.

Mission Tech Q1 revenues declined $85 million YoY due to EUCOM reduction, with MTS backlog and options at $18.5 billion (39% funded), bids awaiting award of $16 billion, and work under contract covering ~91% of 2026 MTS revenue guidance.

Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed across all metrics, with MTS now expected flat to modestly down YoY (offset by mid-teens revenue growth in STS), and revenue phasing of approximately 47% first half / 53% second half.

A potential NASA in-sourcing directive could impact approximately $50-60 million of KBR revenue through 2026, primarily affecting one main contract, and is incorporated as a modest second-half decline in guidance.

The MTS tax-free spin has been pushed from late Q3 2026 to an effective date of January 4, 2027, with public Form 10 filing anticipated in September and two Investor Days planned for the second week of November.

Recurring joint venture contributions (Brown & Root) generated approximately $18 million of EBITDA in Q1, with the company expecting this contribution to tick up modestly as 2026 progresses on strong year-to-date bookings.
Q3 2025 revenues were $950 million, an increase of $62 million or 7% compared to the same period last year.
Q3 2025 net income was a record $32 million compared to $11 million for the same period last year, with net income per diluted share of $2.05 increasing 215% compared to $0.65 last year.
Q3 2025 EBITDA was a record $63 million compared to $37 million for the same period last year.
Total backlog as of September 30, 2025 was $2.66 billion, 2.5% higher than a year ago, consisting of $929 million for T&D and $1.73 billion for C&I.
Q3 2025 operating cash flow was a record $96 million compared to $36 million for the same period last year.
Gross margin was 11.8% for Q3 2025 compared to 8.7% for the same period last year.
Management expects approximately 10% revenue growth for 2026, equally spread between C&I and T&D segments.
The company raised its C&I operating income margin guidance to 5% to 7.5% for 2026, up from the previous 4% to 6% range.
Funded debt-to-EBITDA leverage remained strong at 0.34x as of September 30, 2025, with $400 million in borrowing availability under the credit facility.
T&D operating income margin was 8.2% for Q3 2025 compared to 3.6% for the same period last year, while C&I operating income margin was 6.4% compared to 5.0% last year.
Q4 2025 revenue was $5.3 million, up 128% compared to $2.3 million in Q4 2024, with 16 units sold versus 9 units in the prior year quarter.
Full year 2025 revenue was $13.6 million, up 5% from $12.9 million in 2024, with second-half revenue of $8.7 million significantly exceeding first-half revenue of $4.8 million.

Full year 2026 revenue guidance is $20 million to $22 million, representing approximately 55% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, with revenue expected to progressively strengthen through the quarters.
Q4 2025 gross margin reached 50.9%, representing 1,530 basis points of expansion over Q4 2024, and full year 2026 gross margin guidance is initiated at 50% to 55%.
The company raised over $20 million in equity in October 2025 and an additional $15 million initial tranche from an up to $40 million long-term debt facility, extending cash runway into 2028.

Full year 2026 total cash burn is expected to be $26 million to $28 million, representing a 10% year-over-year decline at the midpoint, with quarterly debt interest payments of approximately $400,000.

The next-generation Swoop system MSRP was increased from $550,000 to $590,000 at the beginning of 2026, with hospitals modeling 1- to 1.5-year ROI timelines versus the 3- to 4-year norm for capital equipment.

The NEURO-PMR study showed portable MRI demonstrated 92% concordance with standard MRI in identifying intracranial pathology in blinded review, increasing to 98% in unblinded paired reviews, with patients 4x more likely to prefer portable MRI over standard MRI.
Only approximately 10% of private neurology practices currently have MRI imaging on-site, representing a large addressable market opportunity with minimal incumbent competition for the Swoop system.

The company is approximately 20% enrolled in its contrast PMR study designed to support a late 2026 FDA submission to expand Swoop's intended use to include gadolinium-based contrast agents, potentially unlocking new applications in neurodegenerative diseases and surgical use.
Q3 2025 product revenue was $22.5 million, an increase of 129% year-over-year and 19% sequentially, marking the company's 19th consecutive quarter of sequential product revenue growth.
The company generated $12.0 million in operating cash flow during Q3 2025, which included a $4.3 million payment from Esteve for international INCRELEX rights.
INCRELEX active patient count grew from 67 patients in December 2024 to approximately 100 patients by August 2025, reaching the company's year-end goal 5 months ahead of schedule.
GALZIN now has over 200 active patients, a number originally set as the year-end 2025 target, and is tracking ahead of deal model expectations.
The company expects Q4 2025 adjusted gross margin of approximately 70%, compared to 45% adjusted gross margin in Q3 which was negatively impacted by INCRELEX ex-U.S. transition costs.
The FDA accepted the ET-600 NDA submission and assigned a February 25, 2026 PDUFA date for what would be the first oral liquid formulation of desmopressin for central diabetes insipidus.

If successful, the INCRELEX label harmonization study could potentially increase the INCRELEX market opportunity roughly fivefold by expanding eligibility to patients with IGF-1 levels between minus 2 and minus 3 standard deviations.

Eton has converted less than 15% of the estimated 5,000 target adrenal insufficiency patients in the U.S. and expects ALKINDI and KHINDIVI combined peak sales of more than $50 million with the current KHINDIVI label.
The company finished Q3 2025 with $37.1 million in cash and reported adjusted EBITDA of $2.9 million, up from $2.0 million in Q3 2024.

Management stated the company is in late-stage discussions with 2 parties on business development opportunities for ultra-rare disease products and expects at least 2 additional product launches next year.
Etsy and Depop combined GMS returned to year-over-year growth in Q3, with consolidated GMS of $2.72 billion exceeding the top end of guidance.
CEO Josh Silverman will transition to Executive Chair effective January 1, 2026, with Kruti Patel Goyal becoming CEO.
Etsy marketplace GMS improved approximately 300 basis points sequentially to $2.43 billion, down 2.4% year-over-year.
Depop GMS grew 39.4% year-over-year to $292 million, with U.S. GMS up 59% year-over-year, and the business is now at an annualized run rate of over $1 billion.
App GMS outperformed non-app GMS by 13 percentage points in Q3, with mobile app's contribution to total GMS increasing to 46% from 42.8% a year ago.
Active buyer count declined 5% year-over-year to 86.6 million on a trailing 12-month basis, with 11.4 million new and reactivated buyers in Q3.
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.4%, with Etsy marketplace margin just shy of 30%.
The company repurchased 2.1 million shares at approximately $120 million in Q3, reducing share count by 17% since December 2023.
Q4 guidance projects consolidated GMS of $3.5 billion to $3.65 billion, with adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 24% due to increased Depop brand marketing investment.
Etsy became the first live partner for OpenAI's instant checkout feature, with early data suggesting buyers from agentic channels have higher purchase intent than those from traditional search.
Q3 comparable sales grew 3% with both Pro and DIY channels delivering positive growth, marking the company's strongest quarter in over 2 years.
Adjusted operating margin expanded 370 basis points year-over-year to 4.4% in Q3.
The company raised nearly $2 billion in cash during Q3 to support its supply chain finance program and asset-backed lending facility.
Same SKU inflation was approximately 3% in Q3, up from about 2% last quarter, and is expected to reach approximately 4% in Q4.
Full year guidance reaffirmed with net sales of $8.55 billion to $8.6 billion and comparable sales growth between 0.7% to 1.3%.
U.S. distribution center count is expected to decline from 38 DCs two years ago to 16 DCs by year-end, with DC productivity improving in the mid-single-digit percentage range.
The company expects to end the year with 33 market hubs, up from 28 at the end of Q3, and is targeting 60 market hubs by mid-2027.
A $28 million noncash charge was recorded related to a supplier bankruptcy, though the company sources less than 2% of cost of goods from this supplier.
Full year free cash flow guidance was revised to negative $90 million to negative $80 million, with capital expenditures reduced to approximately $250 million from prior expectations of $300 million.
Adjusted EPS guidance was updated to $1.75 to $1.85 for the full year, compared to Q3 adjusted diluted EPS of $0.92 versus a loss of $0.05 last year.

Belden announced a definitive agreement to acquire Ruckus Networks from Vistance Networks for approximately $1.85 billion in cash, representing 13x projected 2026 adjusted EBITDA, with closing expected in the second half of 2026.
Q1 2026 revenue was $696 million, up 11% year-over-year (7% organic), and adjusted EPS was $1.77, up 11% year-over-year, both exceeding the high end of guidance.
Q1 adjusted EBITDA was $118 million, up 14% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 40 bps to 17% (approximately 100 bps excluding copper/tariff pass-throughs).
Q2 2026 guidance (excluding Ruckus) calls for revenue of $735–$750 million, GAAP EPS of $1.53–$1.63, and adjusted EPS of $1.95–$2.05.

Ruckus generated $687 million in revenue last year with gross margins above 60% and is expected to deliver high single-digit revenue growth and ~20% EBITDA margins in the first full year of ownership, with immediate accretion to EPS, gross margin, and EBITDA margin.

On a 2025 pro forma basis, Ruckus represents ~20% of combined revenue and raises Belden's solutions mix from 15% to over 20%, accelerating progress toward the 2028 solutions mix target, with management citing ~30% as the right medium-term framework.

Belden secured fully committed debt financing from JPMorgan, plans to pause share repurchases and strategic M&A post-close, and targets net leverage of ~2.9x by year-end 2027 and ~1.5x by year-end 2029.
The combined business will have approximately $650 million of adjusted EBITDA and pro forma unlevered free cash flow of more than $360 million.

Q1 segment performance included mid-single-digit organic growth in automation, double-digit organic growth in smart buildings, mid-single-digit organic growth in broadband, and double-digit growth in data centers, with U.S. revenue up high single digits.

Middle East exposure is less than 5% of total revenue (primarily smart buildings), and Belden has repurchased over $700 million of shares since beginning its 2020 solutions transformation, while growing revenue at a 5% CAGR to $2.7 billion and adjusted EPS at a 12% CAGR to $7.54 in 2025.
Q1 2026 revenue totaled $759.9 million, growing 27% as reported and 25.5% on a constant currency basis versus the prior year quarter.
Fully diluted non-GAAP EPS reached a Q1 record of $1.12, growing 64.7% over the prior year quarter, versus $0.68 in Q1 2025.
Globus raised full year 2026 non-GAAP fully diluted EPS guidance to $4.70–$4.80 (from $4.40–$4.50), while reaffirming revenue guidance of $3.18–$3.22 billion (implying 8.2%–9.6% growth).

U.S. Spine grew 9.6% as reported, marking the third consecutive quarter of ~10% growth and 58 weeks of consecutive growth, with management attributing the majority of growth to share gains against an estimated ~3% market.
Adjusted gross profit margin expanded to 69.2% versus 67.3% in the prior year quarter, with management reiterating a 69%–70% full year 2026 target and a long-term mid-70s goal.

Enabling Technologies revenue was $26.9 million, up 21.1%, but management is shifting the pipeline mix toward leases/rentals versus historical outright sales, which will reduce upfront revenue recognition.

Nevro contributed $82.7 million in Q1, declining 17.1% sequentially from Q4 2025, with management expecting it to potentially worsen before returning to historical run-rate revenue late in the second half of 2026.

Trauma revenue grew 30.4% year-over-year, driven by core trauma share gains, the ANTHEM Elbow plating system, and Precice Limb Lengthening now that manufacturing output has surpassed the former NuVasive facility's output.
International Spine grew 16.4% as reported and 9.8% on a constant currency basis, benefiting from not repeating prior-year supply chain disruptions, with long-term growth expectations of 12%–15%.

Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities rose to $799.3 million (from $629.1 million at year-end 2025) on $202.4 million of operating cash flow, with $390 million remaining under the $500 million share repurchase authorization.
Q1 FY2026 revenue was $3.19 billion, up 59% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating margin at 6.0% and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.38, exceeding outlook.
ZT Systems contributed $1.964 billion in revenue for Q1, coming in at the high end of guidance, with integration on track and margins in line with core Sanmina.
Q2 FY2026 guidance projects revenue of $3.1 billion to $3.4 billion (midpoint $3.25 billion, up 62% YoY) and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.25 to $2.55.
Management stated they are comfortable with the $14 billion consensus revenue estimate for fiscal year 2026.
The company's goal is to double Sanmina revenue in the next 2 years, with AI opportunities on track to deliver $16-plus billion in calendar year 2027.
Non-GAAP pretax ROIC improved to 32.1% from 23.5% in the same period a year ago.
Cash flow from operations was $179 million, with free cash flow of $92 million; the company repurchased 516,000 shares for approximately $79 million.
Core Sanmina business in communications networks and cloud/AI infrastructure grew approximately 20% year-over-year, and is expected to grow high single digits for fiscal year 2026.
Long-term operating margin target is 6% to 7%+, with short-term guidance of 5.7% to 6.0%.
The company is expanding a new state-of-art factory in Houston, Texas for energy business, with plans to ship units in late 2026 and full production in calendar year 2027.
Nephros reported Q3 2025 net revenue of $4.8 million, a 35% increase over Q3 2024 and the company's second highest quarter ever.
Q3 2025 marks Nephros' fifth consecutive quarter of profitability, with net income of $337,000 compared to $183,000 in Q3 2024.
Active customer sites grew sequentially to over 1,650 as of September 30, 2025.
Q3 2025 gross margins were 61%, consistent with Q3 2024, with tariff increases mostly offset by reduced inventory reserve adjustments.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2025 was $418,000 compared to $295,000 in Q3 2024.
Nine-month 2025 sales increased 37% to $14.1 million from $10.3 million in the prior year period.
Nine-month 2025 net income was $1.1 million compared to a net loss of $0.3 million in the prior year period.
Cash balance increased to $5.2 million as of September 30, 2025 from $3.8 million at December 31, 2024, with zero debt.
Nine-month 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $1.4 million compared to $67,000 in the same period of 2024.
Net cash provided by operating activities in Q3 2025 was $99,000, an improvement of $722,000 from net cash used of $623,000 in Q3 2024.
